title: BTatt: factor out common code
description:

notes.body:

it is a false positive of check script @martin.r.mathieson 

but it is not a good idea to call a dissector function proto_tree_add_...

I'll check out the proto_tree_add_time_item tomorrow.

Any suggestion for a better name?

I have amended the commit, changing the name to the one suggested by Alexis
return the offset ? (like other function on this dissector ?)

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12527/diffs?diff_id=813047110&start_sha=0a8cf0490628a2292fa257414a5091831642bf48#c0a73bace44c8ae4ea40321cb8d64f73480c85ea_4776_4776)

I considered that. Personally I am not overly thrilled about constructs  where the invocation is of the form

offset = func(offset);

If one forgets to assign the result of the function then this often leads to a bug.

E.g. consider the case where the last call is to this func and people think: "oh I do not need to consume the function result as I don't use offset any more" And later on for whatever reason a line has to be added (or the code is reorganized) and the offset becomes used adding the assignment may be forgotten.

So that is why I did it this way, but if in wireshark we prefer your suggestion I can modify.

PS: I know there are attributes (at least in gcc) that can warn about unused result but I'm not too keen on using them in portable code.

(oh and a disadvantage of the way I wrote things is the pointer passing a pointer and referencing it insteadd of a scalar.

Since it is a static function I did not check for NULL, so that is an advantage of passing offset back as function result.

Anyway: I can make it either way, just say what is preferred.
it is only for kept the dissector style :)
